title: Peace, Troubled Soul, Whose Plaintive Moan
description: Peace, Troubled Soul, Whose Plaintive Moan in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 269 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Gospel gives Peace and Rest”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Peace, trou-bled soul, whose plain-tive moan Hath taught these rocks the notes of woe; Cease thy com-plaints, sup-press thy groan, And let thy tears for-get to flow: Be-hold the pre-cious balm is found, Which lulls thy pain, which heals thy wound.

lines: Peace, troubled soul, whose plaintive moan
Hath taught these rocks the notes of woe;
Cease thy complaints, suppress thy groan,
And let thy tears forget to flow:
Behold the precious balm is found,
Which lulls thy pain, which heals thy wound.
Come, freely come; by sin oppressed,
Here find thy refuge and thy rest,
And trust the mercy of thy God:
Thy God's thy Father, — glorious word!
Forever love and praise the Lord.
As spring the winter, day the night,
Peace sorrow's gloom shall chase away,
And smiling joy, a seraph bright,
Shall tend thy steps and near thee stay;
Whilst glory weaves th' immortal crown,
And waits to claim thee for her own.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
